approach: Add pure helpers in hestia.rs and call them from `Athena::throughput_review` ahead of the open-request check. Previous per-stage medians are rebuilt from landed jobs without a schema change. The cut now uses ONE set: a new status.rs helper `landed_jobs_among_first(records, n)` ranks ALL landed request jobs (the set `Throughput::compute` counts into `landed_total`, which is what `previous.landings` stores) by (landing end, id), keeps the first `n`, then keeps only those that `landed_jobs` measured. So unmeasured landed jobs no longer shift the cut. `stage_growth` returns stages whose median minutes grew, largest first. `throughput_review` always compares and names grown stages, open design request or not. When the recorded median grew by more than 25% (`SLOWDOWN_RATIO`), it also queues a code-built `Priority: high` request via `StewardRequest::new` and `self.queue`, naming the biggest-growing stage with its measured and previous minutes. The title starts `Throughput slowdown: `, and an open request with that marker suppresses a duplicate. The remark goes into the review `note` (so it reaches the records and the drain line), into a `ui.line`, and into the records commit subject (built by a pure `review_subject`). The drain line is built by a pure `throughput_outcome` that now shows the remark even when a design request was queued. The design-request path (model, one-open-request rule, `throughput_due`, 20% trigger) is unchanged. status.rs also exposes `StageMinutes::median_of` so review and status share one definition of the per-stage median.

decisions.choice: Rebuild the previous per-stage medians with status.rs `landed_jobs_among_first(records, landings)`: sort every landed request job by (landing_end, id) (the key `landed_jobs` sorts by, status.rs 879), take the first `landings` ids, keep the `landed_jobs` entries in that id set, and in hestia.rs `previous_stage_medians` take the newest THROUGHPUT_WINDOW of them and apply `StageMinutes::median_of`. Return None when empty. The 25% test still uses the recorded `previous.window_median_minutes`.
decisions.reason: `previous.landings` is `measured.landed_total` (hestia.rs 1503), which `Throughput::compute` counts over every landed request job (status.rs 886-890). `landed_jobs` drops landed jobs with no invocation (status.rs 853-854, 862). Cutting `landed_jobs` by that count mixes two sets, so the cut drifts forward by the number of unmeasured jobs and the 'previous' window turns into the current one. Ranking over the full landed set removes the drift. `landing_end` is Some for every landed job (a landed job has a closing outcome), so the full-set ranking uses the same landed_at as `landed_jobs`.

rejected.option: Take the first `previous.landings` entries of `landed_jobs` (round 1 plan)
rejected.why: Mixes two sets; the drift is cumulative and ends in an empty growth list while the median rose over 25% (the reported failure, silently).

rejected.option: Add a per-stage-medians field to ThroughputReview
rejected.why: Needs a schema bump (deny_unknown_fields) and gives nothing for old records; the accepted reading and the 'small' default say no schema change.
A landing record can be written after a review that already counted the job (`landing_end` takes the later of outcome and record), so the time cut can disagree with the stored count.

decisions.choice: Queue the slowdown request from code (`StewardRequest::new(Some(Priority::High), ...)` then `self.queue`), before and regardless of the open design request check; never ask the model.
decisions.reason: The failure was a slowdown hidden behind an open request. A deterministic rule that tests drive without the model is the mechanism the 'mechanism' default asks for.

rejected.option: Ask the model to describe the slowdown
rejected.why: Non-deterministic and costs money; the code already has the measured stage and minutes.

rejected.option: Lift the open-request guard for design requests
rejected.why: Would queue a second design proposal; criterion 5 keeps the single open request.

decisions.choice: The slowdown request text does not contain the review id.
decisions.reason: `throughput_followups` treats any landed job whose request text contains a review id as the change that implements that review's proposal (hestia.rs 1382-1393); citing the id would falsely close the prediction made in the same review.

rejected.option: Cite the review id as the design request does

decisions.choice: Dedupe with `SLOWDOWN_MARKER = "Throughput slowdown: "`; generalise `open_throughput_request` (hestia.rs 1353) into `open_request_with_marker(records, marker)` and keep the old name as a one-line call with THROUGHPUT_MARKER.
decisions.reason: The two request kinds are independent; 'Throughput design: ' and 'Throughput slowdown: ' share no prefix, so neither suppresses the other. Stage naming still runs when the request is suppressed.

rejected.why: An open design request would suppress the slowdown request, which is the bug.

decisions.choice: `SLOWDOWN_RATIO = 1.25` with strict `>`; `is_slowdown(previous, current)` is false when previous is not above 0. `WORSEN_RATIO` (1.2) stays as the review trigger.
decisions.reason: Matches `throughput_due`'s 'exactly 20% is not more than 20%' style; a review between 20% and 25% still runs, names stages, queues nothing.

rejected.why: The 20% trigger is out of scope.

decisions.choice: The stage with the largest added minutes (current minus previous median) is 'grew most'; ties keep pipeline order (stable sort); growth under 1e-6 is ignored. If the median grew over 25% but no stage median grew (or the previous window cannot be rebuilt), queue nothing and say so in the note.
decisions.reason: Medians of totals and of stages are not additive, so the case can occur; a request must name a stage and inventing one would be wrong.

rejected.option: Fall back to the stage with the largest current median
rejected.why: Names a stage that did not grow.

decisions.choice: Carry the finding in the existing `note` string (appended after any existing note with '; ') and in a `ui.line`. A queued slowdown job id appears in the note as `slowdown request {job} queued at high priority`. No record field is added.
decisions.reason: Existing tests assert `note.contains("still open")` and `starts_with("no proposal")`; appending keeps them true. `review_passes` receives only the `ThroughputReview`, so the note is the carrier to the drain line.

decisions.choice: Fix the two reader-facing strings that would otherwise be wrong. (a) Extract the commit subject (hestia.rs 1519-1532) into a pure `review_subject(median, design: Option<&JobId>, slowdown: Option<&JobId>) -> String` that names the design request, the slowdown request, both, or 'no request queued'; `throughput_review` keeps the slowdown job in a local `slowdown_job`. (b) Extract the outcome text in `review_passes` (hestia.rs 1851-1860) into a pure `throughput_outcome(&ThroughputReview) -> String`; in the design-request-queued branch it appends ` · {note}` when the note is not empty, and the other branches already print `r.note`.
decisions.reason: Without (a) the record history would say 'no request queued' for a review that queued one; without (b) the drain line would not show the slowdown when a design request was queued. Pure functions can be tested without driving the whole drain.

rejected.option: Leave the subject and drain line alone
rejected.why: The subject would be false and the drain line would hide the flag.
It also runs the backfill, label and spec passes, which need more fixtures; the pure outcome function is the logic that changes.

decisions.choice: Extract the per-stage median closure in `Throughput::compute` (status.rs 905-915) into `StageMinutes::median_of(window: &[LandedJob])` and use it in both places.
decisions.reason: One definition so the review compares like with like; `compute`'s output does not change.

rejected.why: The two could drift apart with no test failing.

decisions.reason: The brief lists records.rs; the `note` doc should say it can hold the slowdown remark. No field, schema or validation change, so the round-trip test stays valid.

rejected.why: The `note` doc would describe only proposal-less reasons.

risks.risk: The rebuilt previous window can still differ from what the previous review saw, because a landing record written after that review moves a job's `landed_at` and so its rank.
risks.mitigation: The unmeasured-job drift, which was cumulative, is gone because the cut is made over the same set the count came from. The remaining error is limited to jobs whose landing time moved after the review. The doc comment says the window is a reconstruction. The 25% decision uses the recorded median, not the reconstruction. If the window comes out empty, the note says the previous stages could not be rebuilt.

risks.risk: The median of totals can exceed 1.25 times the previous one while no stage median grew, so no stage can be named.
risks.mitigation: Queue nothing and say in the note that the median grew over 25% but no stage's median did; a `stage_growth` test covers it. Naming a stage that did not grow was rejected.

risks.risk: A slowdown request is queued on every review while the slowdown persists.
risks.mitigation: An open request with the slowdown marker holds back another, and each comparison is against the previous review. Test A covers the second review.

risks.risk: The slowdown request could be mistaken for the change that implements a design proposal made in the same review.
risks.mitigation: The request text omits the review id, and the pure builder test asserts that.

risks.risk: `athena plan` or the admission scan refuses the new request.
risks.mitigation: It is built with `StewardRequest::new`, which checks plan acceptance and applies boundary rewording, and `queue` applies `refuse_banned_input`. Stage lists stay on one line with no bullet-like lines. The builder test checks `request_text_acceptance`.

risks.risk: The test fixtures do not reach a window median of exactly 60.
risks.mitigation: Use 9 old and 11 new jobs in the newest 20, so the median is the new value, and assert `window_median_minutes` before the other assertions.

risks.risk: A test fixture for unmeasured landed jobs does not count as landed or measured as expected.
risks.mitigation: `timed_job` leaves out zero-minute stages, so `StageMinutes::default()` gives a landed job with only a request and an outcome. `Throughput::compute` counts it in `landed_total` and `landed_jobs` drops it (status.rs 862). demonstrations.method: Two new tests drive `Athena::throughput_review` over committed records, with an open `Throughput design: ` request and a model that must not be called. Test A (`a_median_rise_from_25_to_60_with_a_design_request_open_names_the_grown_stages_and_queues_a_high_request`): ten 25-minute jobs (producer 25) plus `earlier_review(10, 25.0)` plus the open design request job, then 11 jobs of 60 minutes (producer 45, checks 10, verifier 5). Test B (`unmeasured_landed_jobs_before_the_earlier_review_do_not_hide_the_growth`): twelve landed jobs with no invocation (`timed_job` with `StageMinutes::default()`) landing first, then ten 25-minute jobs, `earlier_review(22, 25.0)`, the open design request, then 11 jobs of 60 minutes. A naive cut of `landed_jobs` by 22 would take all 21 measured jobs and report nothing. Also a status.rs test of `landed_jobs_among_first`, and a pure test of `review_subject`.
demonstrations.observes: Both tests: `review.window_median_minutes == 60.0`; the model call log is empty; `note` contains 'still open' and the names producer, checks and verifier (producer 25.0 to 45.0 first); exactly one open request starts `Throughput slowdown: `, its `priority()` is `Priority::High`, and the queued text begins `Priority: high` and has the stage names and minutes; `note` contains `slowdown request <job> queued`; the `Lines` UI got a line with the stage names. Test B also asserts `previous_stage_medians(...).producer == 25.0` for the rebuilt window. `review_subject` with a slowdown job and no design job contains the job id and not 'no request queued'. A second review with 10 more, slower jobs while the slowdown request is open names the grown stage and queues no second one.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the comparison ahead of the open-request branch, the note is only the 'still open' text and no `Throughput slowdown: ` request exists. With the round-1 cut, Test B finds no grown stage and queues nothing. With the old subject code, the `review_subject` assertion fails.

demonstrations.command: cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings && cargo test --locked
demonstrations.observes: All three exit 0. `git diff --stat` lists only hestia.rs, status.rs, records.rs (doc comments only), docs/design/hestia.md and CHANGELOG.md; no athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflow file.
demonstrations.fails_without: A formatting, clippy or test failure fails the command; a governance file change shows in the diff.
demonstrations.seam: None: cargo and git run on the working tree.

demonstrations.method: Read the diff of the hestia.rs module comment (lines 43-52) and docs/design/hestia.md section 12, and the CHANGELOG entry.
demonstrations.observes: The module comment, the doc comments on `SLOWDOWN_RATIO`, `stage_growth`, `previous_stage_medians`, `slowdown_request`, and section 12 state: every review compares the latest median with the previous review's, even with a design request open; the previous stage medians are rebuilt from the same set of landed jobs the stored count came from; grown stages are named; more than 25% queues a high-priority request naming the biggest-growing stage and its measured minutes; one open slowdown request holds back another. The CHANGELOG Unreleased entry names the behavior.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the doc changes the module comment and section 12 would still describe only the 10-landing and 20% triggers.
demonstrations.seam: None: a content check of the diff.

open_questions: User: records.rs is a listed deliverable but this plan changes only its doc comments, because the previous stage medians are rebuilt from landed jobs. Should the review store per-stage medians in `athena.throughput-review/1` (a schema change) instead? The plan assumes not, as the accepted reading says.
